How the forecast works

Every team gets an attack and a defence rating from a Dixon-Coles model fitted on Serie A results since 2018/19. Each past match is fitted to a blend: — comes from the goals its closing betting odds implied, and the rest from the pitch, where this season's matches count as — expected goals (xG) and the rest real goals. Older matches count less: a match loses half its weight after — days. Playing at home is worth — goals compared with playing away. Promoted teams start from the average rating of past promoted sides.

The rest of the season is then played out many times. In each run, every team's rating moves by a random amount, sized to how much ratings drift during a season. Ties are broken on goal difference and goals scored. Serie A's head-to-head rule and its play-offs for the title and for the last relegation place are not modelled.

Backtest: before every matchday of 2023/24 to 2025/26, the model was refitted using only matches already played. RPS (ranked probability score) and log loss measure the error of the home/draw/away probabilities. Lower is better. Because the ratings use past closing odds, the model is not independent of the bookmakers it is compared with.
